input.answer:
I can't tell you whether to buy or rent. That depends on your savings, income, job stability, how long you'll stay, and your risk tolerance, and it's personal advice, which is outside what I can give. A financial adviser or a mortgage broker can work through those factors with you.

What I can offer is one relevant data point. For Toronto, StatCan's New Housing Price Index (total, house and land) fell from 110.4 in September 2025 to 105.0 in September 2026: (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4 = −4.9%. This covers newly built homes only, not resale prices, and it says nothing about rents, mortgage rates, or your own costs. I could not retrieve Toronto rent series: the rent table I found (46-10-0092) was not available in the snapshot, so I have no rent figures to compare against.

answer_values.label: change_pct
answer_values.description: Percent change in Toronto new housing price index (total, house and land), Sept 2025 to Sept 2026: (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4
